Commentary.Commentary: There is still a steady drizzle, not too heavy but enough to delay proceeds. The forecast is overcast but we will hopefully resume soon.
1955 IST update - The latest news is that the play resumes at 2010 IST.
Unfortunately, the resumption has been delayed due to a persistent drizzle. However, the rain has passed us and the radar looks clear. We are set for resumption at 1955 IST.

The pitch looks flat and after what happened in the 2nd ODI, England will not be too perturbed with this target, especially with Mathews not fit to bowl. The run chase is scheduled to begin at 1915 IST but as we type, covers are being brought on to the field. Fingers crossed, hopefully we will see a resumption on time.

Chris Woakes led the bowling attack, picking up three scalps with an economy rate of 3.4, including a maiden, after his full 10 overs. Plunkett matched him with three wickets of his own and exceptional bowling figures as well. Willey and Jordan also did a good job, taking one wicket each.

England carried themselves well in the bowling department, doing well to restrict the Lankans on a scoring ground and taking crucial wickets whenever the tourists looked to settle in. They also distinguished themselves well on the field, assisting the bowlers in nearly all the wickets taken.

Chandimal was dismissed in the 36th over but Mathews went on to score his 38th ODI half century and the third one after Mendis and Chandimal. Tharanga brought some stability to the other end for Mathews and held on after Mathews departed. Despite the tail-enders leaving him stranded, Tharanga was able to notch up 40 runs off 33 balls.

That ends the batting innings for Sri Lanka with a target of 249. It was a disappointing and rather slow innings for the visitors as they struggled and failed to cross 250. After Gunathilaka's early dismissal, Perera and Mendis got them off to a slow start, bringing up 29 runs in around 8 overs. Once Plunkett picked up the scalp of Perera, Chandimal was ushered in and what followed was a 56-run partnership off a slightly faster 78 balls. Plunkett struck again, bringing down Mendis and ending the stand up but Mathews came in and picked up where Mendis left off. What followed was the biggest partnership of the innings, an 80-run partnership off 87 balls.

Starts with a length ball around middle and leg, Perera misses his flick and the ball goes off his thigh pads towards square leg. A leg bye taken.
The players are out in the middle. Kusal Perera and Danushka Gunathilaka are the openers for Sri Lanka. David Willey will start off proceedings against Kusal. Here we go...

TEAM NEWS - Both sides have a change each. For England, Moeen Ali has been rested and CHRIS JORDAN comes in his place. The Lankans bring back DASUN SHANAKA for Suraj Randiv. Both Mathews and Chandimal are playing but will do only department properly - bat.
TOSS - The news from out in the middle is that ENGLAND HAVE WON THE TOSS AND ELECTED TO CHASE. So for the third game on the trot, Sri Lanka will be batting first.

Test series gone. Super Series gone, with England opening a 13-3 advantage and just 4 matches left in the tour. What is left then? Well, if Sri Lanka manage to win three games on the trot, they can win the ODI series. That should motivate them when they take on the hosts in the third ODI at Bristol. Hello and a warm welcome to what we hope will be a good encounter.
